answer: Attention-escrow release schedule. Each identity earns spendable credits only by holding a session open across random checkpoints; credits unlock at dawn after the last checkpoint. An attacker running many clones must staff every session continuously, paying real attention cost per clone through the night, since idle sessions forfeit escrow. A dune of cheap registrations yields nothing without sustained presence. Sybil cost scales with hours held, not identities created, and a stray zephyr of automation fails checkpoint probes.
